[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Dockerization and Container Best Practices for Flask Applications"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Containerizing a Flask application allows you to package your code, runtime, system tools, and libraries into a single isolated unit. This tutorial covers how to create an optimized Docker image for Flask and follow industry-standard container best practices."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Basic knowledge of Python and Flask."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Docker installed on your local machine."},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Creating a Basic Flask Application"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create a project directory and add a simple application file named app.py."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"from flask import Flask

app = Flask(__name__)

@app.route('/')
def hello_world():
    return 'Hello, Dockerized Flask!'

if __name__ == '__main__':
    app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=5000)"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Managing Dependencies"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Generate a requirements.txt file to specify your Python dependencies. For production, include a production WSGI server like Gunicorn."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"Flask==3.0.0
Gunicorn==21.2.0"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Writing an Optimized Dockerfile"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create a file named Dockerfile in your root directory. Follow best practices such as using slim base images, multi-stage builds where necessary, and running containers as a non-root user."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"FROM python:3.11-slim

WORKDIR /app

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY . .

RUN useradd -u 1000 appuser && chown -R appuser:appuser /app
USER appuser

EXPOSE 5000

CMD ["gunicorn", "--bind", "0.0.0.0:5000", "app:app"]"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Using .dockerignore"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"To keep your build context small and secure, always include a .dockerignore file in your project root."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"__pycache__
*.pyc
*.pyo
*.pyd
.env
.git
.gitignore
venv/
Dockerfile

docker run -p 5000:5000 flask-app"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Container Best Practices Summary"},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Never run your application as the root user inside the container."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use official slim or alpine base images to reduce attack surface and image size."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid using the built-in Flask development server in production; use Gunicorn or uWSGI instead."},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Leverage build caches effectively by copying requirements.txt before copying the rest of the source code."}]
